nodes.name: Polar decomposition of scale-homogeneous measures on R^d
nodes.statement: A scale-homogeneous measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is finite outside a neighborhood of the origin can be represented in polar coordinates as the product of a probability measure on the unit sphere (the directional or angular component) and a scale-homogeneous measure on the positive reals (the radial component).
assumptions: A scale-homogeneous measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is finite outside a neighborhood of the origin
conclusions: can be represented in polar coordinates as the product of a probability measure on the unit sphere (the directional or angular component) and a scale-homogeneous measure on the positive reals (the radial component)
nodes.statement_short: A homogeneous measure on R^d finite away from 0 is a product of an angular probability measure and a radial homogeneous measure.

nodes.name: Form of scale-homogeneous measures on the positive reals
nodes.statement: A nontrivial scale-homogeneous measures on the positive reals that is finite outside neighborhoods of the origin is necessarily of the form $c \, \alpha \, t^{-(\alpha + 1)} \, dt$ for some constants $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$.
assumptions: A nontrivial scale-homogeneous measures on the positive reals that is finite outside neighborhoods of the origin
conclusions: is necessarily of the form $c \, \alpha \, t^{-(\alpha + 1)} \, dt$ for some constants $c > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$

nodes.name: LePage series representation
nodes.statement: Such a polar decomposition of the L\'evy measure leads to a representation of stable random elements as the sum of a series obtained from a sequence of i.i.d. random elements scaled by the points of a Poisson process on the positive real line with intensity measure of the form $\alpha \, t^{-(\alpha + 1)} \, dt$ or, equivalently by points of the form $\Gamma_k^{-\frac{1}{\alpha}}$, where $(\Gamma_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ are the points of a unit intensity Poisson process on the positive real line. Such a representation was first obtained in \cite{lep:wood:zin81} for Euclidean space and since then it and its various extensions have been called the {\em LePage series} representation.
nodes.statement_short: Representation of a stable element as a series of i.i.d. elements scaled by Gamma_k^{-1/alpha}, Gamma_k unit-rate Poisson points.

nodes.name: Scaling
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{X}$ be a measurable space with a $\sigma$-algebra $\mathfrak{B}$, and let $(x,t)\mapsto tx\in\mathbb{X}$ be a \emph{pairing} of $x\in\mathbb{X}$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}:=(0,\infty)$ which is $\mathfrak{B} \otimes \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}_{++}) / \mathfrak{B}$-measurable, where $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}_{++})$ is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{R}_{++}$. Assume that this pairing is an {\em action} of the group $\mathbb{R}_{++}$ (where the group operation is the usual multiplication of real numbers) on $\mathbb{X}$; that is, for all $t,s>0$ and $x\in\mathbb{X}$, $t(sx)=(ts)x$ and $1 x = x$. We refer to such a pairing as a \emph{scaling}.
differentia: is an {\em action} of the group $\mathbb{R}_{++}$
nodes.statement_short: A scaling is a measurable action of the multiplicative group of positive reals on a measurable space.

nodes.name: Scaled sets are measurable
nodes.statement: For $B\in\mathfrak{B}$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$, set $tB:=\{tx:\; x\in B\}$. The measurability of the map $x\mapsto tx$ for each $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$ yields that $s B=\{x:\; (s^{-1})x\in B\}\in\mathfrak{B}$ for all $B\in\mathfrak{B}$ and $s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$.

equivalent_conditions: The measure $\nu$ is a nontrivial $\alpha$-homogeneous measure with \begin{equation} \nu(U_k)<\infty,\qquad k\in\mathbb{N}\,. \end{equation}

The measure $\nu$ is the push-forward of the measure $\pi\otimes\theta_\alpha$ by the map $(x,t)\mapsto tx$, where $\pi$ is a probability measure on $\mathbb{X}$ such that \begin{equation} \int_0^\infty \pi(tU_k)t^{\alpha-1} \, dt < \infty,\qquad k\in\mathbb{N}, \end{equation} and $\theta_\alpha$ is the measure on $\mathbb{R}_{++}$ given by $\theta_\alpha(dt) := \alpha t^{-(\alpha+1)} \, dt$.

For a probability measure $\pi$ on $\mathbb{X}$ such that \eqref{eq:pi-Sk} holds, \begin{equation} \nu(B) = \alpha \int_0^\infty \pi(t B) \, t^{\alpha-1} \, dt \end{equation} for all $B \in \mathfrak{B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Under Assumption A, a nontrivial alpha-homogeneous measure finite on the U_k is exactly the push-forward of pi x theta_alpha under (x,t)->tx.

nodes.name: Orbit and transversal
nodes.statement: The {\em orbits} of the action of the group $\mathbb{R}_{++}$ on $\mathbb{X}$ are the sets of the form $\{t x : t \in \mathbb{R}_{++}\}$ for some $x \in \mathbb{X}$. The orbits are the equivalence classes for the equivalence relation on $\mathbb{X}$ where we declare $x$ and $y$ to be equivalent if $y = t x$ for some $t \in \mathbb{R}_{++}$. nodes.statement_short: Orbits are sets {tx: t>0}; a measurable set meeting each orbit in exactly one point is a transversal.

nodes.name: Transversal constructed from vanishing functions
nodes.statement: If $h_n(tx)\to 0$ as $t\downarrow0$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then it is not necessary to require Assumption~\ref{assumption:X} in Theorem~\ref{thr:general-polar}. A measurable transversal can be constructed as follows. For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let \begin{displaymath} W_n:=\{x\in\mathbb{X}:\; h_k(x)=0,k<n,\; h_n(x)\neq 0\}. \end{displaymath} Next, partition $W_n$ into measurable sets \begin{align*} W_{nj}&:=\{x\in W_n:\; \sup_{t>0} h_n(tx)\in(2^{-j},2^{-j+1}]\},\qquad j\geq 1,\\ W_{n0}&:=\{x\in W_n:\; \sup_{t>0} h_n(tx)>1\}. \end{align*} Finally, define \begin{displaymath} \tau_{nj}(x):=\inf\{t>0:\; h_n(tx)>2^{-j}\},\qquad x\in W_{nj}, \end{displaymath} and \begin{displaymath} S_{nj}:=\{\tau_{nj}(x)^{-1}x:\; x\in W_{nj}\}. \end{displaymath} Then $\mathbb{S}:=\bigcup_{n,j\in\mathbb{N}} S_{nj}$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assumption:X} in the complement of the set $\{x\in\mathbb{X}:\; h_n(x)=0,n\in\mathbb{N}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: If all h_n(tx)->0 as t->0, a measurable transversal can be built from level crossings of h_n, so Assumption B is not needed.
nodes.label: rem:sphere-from-h

nodes.name: Polar representation
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thr:general-polar} asserts that an $\alpha$-homogeneous measure $\nu$ is the push-forward of the measure $\pi\otimes \theta_\alpha$ under the map $(x,t)\mapsto tx$ from $\mathbb{X} \times \mathbb{R}_{++}$ to $\mathbb{X}$. In this case we say that $\nu$ admits a \emph{polar representation}. It follows from the proof that we may replace $\mathbb{X}$ by a subset that is invariant under the action of $\mathbb{R}_{++}$ in such a way that the probability measure $\pi$ assigns all of its mass to a transversal.
nodes.statement_short: Names the conclusion of Theorem 2.15: nu admits a polar representation pi x theta_alpha, with pi carried by a transversal.

nodes.name: Convex cone
nodes.statement: A \emph{convex cone} $\mathbb{K}$ is an abelian measurable semigroup with neutral element $\mathbf{e}$ and a scaling $(x,a) \mapsto a x$ by $\mathbb{R}_{++}$ that has the properties \begin{align*} a(x+y)&=ax+ay,\qquad a>0,\;x,y\in\mathbb{K},\\ a\mathbf{e}&=\mathbf{e},\qquad a>0. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.genus: abelian measurable semigroup with neutral element
also_stated_at: A {\em convex cone} is a semigroup equipped with a scaling, that is, with an action of the group of positive real numbers that interacts suitably with the semigroup operation.

nodes.name: Simplest convex cones
nodes.statement: The simplest examples of convex cones are $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}_+^d$ with the usual scaling by $\mathbb{R}_{++}$, but there are many other examples, some of which we will recall later in this paper.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: No second distributivity law
nodes.statement: In contrast to the many classical studies of convex cones that are convex subsets of vector spaces over the reals which are closed under multiplication by nonnegative scalars (see, for example, \cite{fuc:lus81}), we do not assume the validity of the second distributivity law; that is, we do not require that $ax+bx=(a+b)x$ for $a,b > 0$ and $x \in \mathbb{K}$. Stable random elements of convex cones have been studied in \cite{dav:mol:zuy08} under the assumptions that the scaling is jointly continuous and that $\mathbb{K}':=\mathbb{K}\setminus\{\mathbf{e}\}$ is a Polish space.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Unlike classical cones, $ax+bx=(a+b)x$ is not assumed; cites earlier work under Polish and continuity assumptions.

nodes.name: Involution
nodes.statement: An \emph{involution} is a measurable map $x\mapsto x^*$ satisfying $(x+y)^*=x^*+y^*$, $(ax)^*=ax^*$, and $(x^*)^*=x$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{K}$ and $a>0$. We assume that $\mathbb{K}$ is equipped with an involution.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Bounded semicharacter
nodes.statement: A measurable function $\chi$ that maps $\mathbb{K}$ into the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ in the complex plane is called a {\em bounded semicharacter} (or, more briefly, a \emph{character}) if $\chi(\mathbf{e})=1$, $\chi(x+y)=\chi(x)\chi(y)$, and $\chi(x^*)=\overline{\chi(x)}$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{K}$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.genus: measurable function $\chi$ that maps $\mathbb{K}$ into the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$

nodes.name: Characters form a convex cone
nodes.statement: The family of all characters form a convex cone when equipped with pointwise multiplication as the semigroup operation, the topology of pointwise convergence, the neutral element $\mathbf{1}$ being the character identically equal to $1$, the involution being the complex conjugate, and the scaling defined by $(a\chi)(x):=\chi(ax)$, $x\in\mathbb{K}$, $a>0$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Separating family of characters
nodes.statement: We assume in the following that there exists a \emph{separating} family $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ of characters in the usual sense that for each $x\neq y$ there exists $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ such that $\chi(x)\neq\chi(y)$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Characters generate the sigma-algebra and form a semigroup
nodes.statement: We also assume that the characters in $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ generate the $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{K}$ and that the family $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ is closed under taking finite products, contains the constant function $1$, and so is a semigroup itself.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Laplace transform
nodes.statement: The distribution of a $\mathbb{K}$-valued random element $\xi$ is determined by its \emph{Laplace transform} $\mathbb{E}\chi(\xi)$, $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$, (see, for example, \cite[Th.~5.4]{dav:mol:zuy08}).
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Symmetric random element
nodes.statement: A random element $\xi$ is said to be \emph{symmetric} if $\xi\overset{d}{\sim}\xi^*$, that is, $\xi$ coincides in distribution with its involution.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Laplace transform of a symmetric element is real
nodes.statement: The Laplace transform of a symmetric random element takes only real values.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
conclusions: takes only real values

nodes.name: Identity involution makes every element symmetric
nodes.statement: If the involution is the identity, then all random elements are symmetric.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
conclusions: all random elements are symmetric

nodes.name: Strictly $\alpha$-stable random element
nodes.statement: A random element $\xi$ in $\mathbb{K}$ is said to be \emph{strictly $\alpha$-stable} if \begin{equation} a^{1/\alpha}\xi'+b^{1/\alpha}\xi'' \overset{d}{\sim} (a+b)^{1/\alpha}\xi\,,\qquad a,b>0\,, \end{equation} where $\xi'$ and $\xi''$ are i.i.d. copies of $\xi$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Strict stability relation
nodes.statement: a^{1/\alpha}\xi'+b^{1/\alpha}\xi'' \overset{d}{\sim} (a+b)^{1/\alpha}\xi\,,\qquad a,b>0\,,
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: Eq:stable

nodes.name: Alternative definition of strict stability
nodes.statement: An alternative definition of strictly stable random elements that coincides with the above for $\mathbb{R}^d$ (and in many other situations) requires that, for all $n\geq2$, there exists $a_n>0$ such that $\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_n\overset{d}{\sim} a_n\xi$, where $\xi,\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n$ are i.i.d. and $n\geq2$. While \eqref{Eq:stable} implies this condition immediately, extra assumptions related to the semicontinuity property of characters and the continuity of the scaling operation are needed for the equivalence of the two definitions, see \cite[Th.~5.16]{dav:mol:zuy08}. The major step is to establish that $a_n=n^{1/\alpha}$, after which \eqref{Eq:stable} follows easily.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Laplace transform of infinitely divisible elements
nodes.statement: A strictly $\alpha$-stable $\xi$ is always \emph{infinitely divisible} and so its Laplace transform satisfies \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}\chi(\xi)=\exp\{-\varphi(\chi)\},\qquad \chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}\,, \end{equation} for a negative definite complex-valued function $\varphi$ on $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ with $\mathrm{Re}\,\varphi\in[0,\infty]$ and $\varphi(\mathbf{1})=0$, see \cite[Th.~3.2.2, Prop.~4.3.1]{ber:c:r}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
conclusions: is always \emph{infinitely divisible}
\mathbb{E}\chi(\xi)=\exp\{-\varphi(\chi)\},\qquad \chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}\,,
nodes.statement_short: Strictly stable elements are infinitely divisible, with Laplace transform exp(-phi) for a negative definite phi.

nodes.name: Laplace exponent representation
nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\chi(\xi)=\exp\{-\varphi(\chi)\},\qquad \chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}\,,
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: Eq:Laplace-exponent

nodes.name: Laplace exponent
nodes.statement: The function $\varphi$ is called the \emph{Laplace exponent} of $\xi$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Lévy measure
nodes.statement: A Laplace exponent is associated with a unique \emph{L\'evy measure} $\nu$, a Radon measure on the semigroup of all bounded characters on $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$, see \cite{ber:c:r}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.genus: a Radon measure on the semigroup of all bounded characters on $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$

nodes.name: Lévy measure supported and sigma-finite on K'
nodes.statement: In the following we always assume that the L\'evy measure is supported by $\mathbb{K}':=\mathbb{K}\setminus\{\mathbf{e}\}$ canonically embedded into the semigroup of all bounded semicharacters on $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ and that it is $\sigma$-finite on $\mathbb{K}'$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Admits a Lévy measure
nodes.statement: In this case we say that $\xi$ \emph{admits a L\'evy measure}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Lévy measure integrability condition
nodes.statement: The L\'evy measure $\nu$ satisfies \begin{equation} \int_{\mathbb{K}'}(1-\mathrm{Re}\, \chi(x))\,\nu(dx)<\infty \end{equation} for all $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
conclusions: \int_{\mathbb{K}'}(1-\mathrm{Re}\, \chi(x))\,\nu(dx)<\infty

nodes.name: Lévy measure integrability
nodes.statement: \int_{\mathbb{K}'}(1-\mathrm{Re}\, \chi(x))\,\nu(dx)<\infty
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: eq:lev-mes

nodes.name: Poisson process of the Lévy measure; no deterministic, Gaussian or idempotent components
nodes.statement: The measure $\nu$ is the intensity measure of a Poisson process $\{\eta_i: i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ on $\mathbb{K}'$, and the appropriately defined (if necessary using principal values and compensating terms) sum of the points $\eta_i$ yields an infinitely divisible random element that is said to not have deterministic, Gaussian or idempotent components.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
definiendum: not have deterministic, Gaussian or idempotent components

nodes.name: Non-vanishing Laplace transform (Lemma 3.9)
nodes.statement: Assume for some $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ that \begin{equation} \liminf_{t\downarrow0} \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(tx)>0 \end{equation} for all $x\in\mathbb{K}$. If $\xi$ is a strictly $\alpha$-stable random element, then $\mathbb{E}\chi(\xi)\neq 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
conclusions: $\mathbb{E}\chi(\xi)\neq 0$
nodes.label: lemma:non-zero

nodes.name: Positivity of liminf of characters
nodes.statement: \liminf_{t\downarrow0} \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(tx)>0
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: Eq:lim-chi-positive

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.9
nodes.statement: Since $-1 \le \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t x) \le 1$ for all $t > 0$ and $x \in \mathbb{K}$, it follows from the assumption \eqref{Eq:lim-chi-positive} and Fatou's Lemma that \begin{equation} 0 < \mathbb{E} \left[\liminf_{t\downarrow0} \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t\xi)\right] \le \liminf_{t\downarrow0} \mathbb{E} \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t\xi). \end{equation} By the stability property of $\xi$, $\mathbb{E}\chi(\xi) = (\mathbb{E}\chi(n^{-1/\alpha}\xi))^n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and so $\mathbb{E}\chi(\xi) = 0$ would imply that $\mathbb{E}\chi(n^{-1/\alpha}\xi)=0$ and hence $\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{Re}\,\chi(n^{-1/\alpha}\xi)=0$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, but this contradicts \eqref{eq:Fatou_for_char}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Fatou's lemma gives a positive liminf; stability writes E chi(xi) as an n-th power, so vanishing would contradict it.

nodes.name: Fatou bound for characters
nodes.statement: 0 < \mathbb{E} \left[\liminf_{t\downarrow0} \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t\xi)\right] \le \liminf_{t\downarrow0} \mathbb{E} \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t\xi).
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: eq:Fatou_for_char

nodes.name: Lévy measure is homogeneous (Lemma 3.10)
nodes.statement: Assume that \eqref{Eq:lim-chi-positive} holds for all $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$. Then the L\'evy measure of a strictly $\alpha$-stable random element is an $\alpha$-homogeneous measure on $\mathbb{K}'$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
conclusions: the L\'evy measure of a strictly $\alpha$-stable random element is an $\alpha$-homogeneous measure on $\mathbb{K}'$
nodes.label: lemma:homogeneous

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.10
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{Eq:stable} that \begin{displaymath} \varphi(a^{1/\alpha}\chi)+\varphi(b^{1/\alpha}\chi) =\varphi((a+b)^{1/\alpha}\chi),\quad a,b>0\,, \end{displaymath} where the Laplace exponent $\varphi$ of the strictly stable random element $\xi$ is finite by Lemma~\ref{lemma:non-zero}. Since $(x,a)\mapsto ax$ is a jointly measurable map, the function $a \mapsto \mathbb{E}\chi(a\xi)$ is measurable by Fubini's theorem. Therefore, \begin{equation} \varphi(a\chi)=a^\alpha\varphi(\chi),\qquad a>0. \end{equation} The random element $a\xi$ is also infinitely divisible and its L\'evy measure is $B \mapsto \nu(aB)$ for measurable subsets $B\subseteq\mathbb{K}'$. By \eqref{eq:phi-homogeneous}, the L\'evy measure of $a\xi$ is $a^\alpha\nu$. Since the L\'evy measure is unique, we obtain \eqref{eq:nu-x-homogeneous}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Stability makes the Laplace exponent alpha-homogeneous in the scaling; uniqueness of the Lévy measure transfers this to nu.

nodes.name: Additivity of the Laplace exponent
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{Eq:stable} that \begin{displaymath} \varphi(a^{1/\alpha}\chi)+\varphi(b^{1/\alpha}\chi) =\varphi((a+b)^{1/\alpha}\chi),\quad a,b>0\,, \end{displaymath} where the Laplace exponent $\varphi$ of the strictly stable random element $\xi$ is finite by Lemma~\ref{lemma:non-zero}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Stability gives an additive functional equation for phi, finite by Lemma 3.9.

nodes.name: Homogeneity of the Laplace exponent
nodes.statement: Since $(x,a)\mapsto ax$ is a jointly measurable map, the function $a \mapsto \mathbb{E}\chi(a\xi)$ is measurable by Fubini's theorem. Therefore, \begin{equation} \varphi(a\chi)=a^\alpha\varphi(\chi),\qquad a>0. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Measurability via Fubini turns the Cauchy equation into phi(a chi)=a^alpha phi(chi).

nodes.name: Transfer to the Lévy measure
nodes.statement: The random element $a\xi$ is also infinitely divisible and its L\'evy measure is $B \mapsto \nu(aB)$ for measurable subsets $B\subseteq\mathbb{K}'$. By \eqref{eq:phi-homogeneous}, the L\'evy measure of $a\xi$ is $a^\alpha\nu$. Since the L\'evy measure is unique, we obtain \eqref{eq:nu-x-homogeneous}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Compare Lévy measures of a xi and use uniqueness.

nodes.name: Homogeneity of the Laplace exponent
nodes.statement: \varphi(a\chi)=a^\alpha\varphi(\chi),\qquad a>0.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: eq:phi-homogeneous

nodes.name: LePage representation of strictly stable elements (Theorem 3.11)
nodes.statement:
Let $\xi$ be a strictly stable random element that admits a $\sigma$-finite L'evy measure $
u$. Assume that there is a countable, closed under finite products, separating family of characters $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ such that $t \mapsto \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(tx)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$, is right- (or left-) continuous for all $x\in\mathbb{K}'$ and $\chi \in \hat{\mathbb{K}}$. Assume also that Assumption~ef{assumption:X} holds and \eqref{Eq:lim-chi-positive} holds for all $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$. Then $
u$ admits the polar representation $\pi\otimes	heta_\alpha$, where $\pi$ is a probability measure on $\mathbb{K}'$ satisfying  egin{equation} \int_0^\infty \mathbb{E}[1-\mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t\varepsilon)] t^{-(\alpha+1)} \, dt <\infty, \qquad \chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}. \end{equation} The Poisson process with intensity measure $
u$ can be represented as $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$, where $\{\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. copies of a random element $\varepsilon$ in $\mathbb{K}'$ with distribution $\pi$, and $\{\Gamma_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ are successive points of a unit intensity Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}_+$. If $\xi$ is symmetric, then $\varepsilon$ can also be chosen to have a symmetric distribution.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
assumptions: $\xi$ be a strictly stable random element that admits a $\sigma$-finite L\'evy measure $\nu$

there is a countable, closed under finite products, separating family of characters $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ such that $t \mapsto \mathrm{Re}\,\chi(tx)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$, is right- (or left-) continuous for all $x\in\mathbb{K}'$ and $\chi \in \hat{\mathbb{K}}$
conclusions: $\nu$ admits the polar representation $\pi\otimes\theta_\alpha$, where $\pi$ is a probability measure on $\mathbb{K}'$ satisfying
The Poisson process with intensity measure $\nu$ can be represented as $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$
If $\xi$ is symmetric, then $\varepsilon$ can also be chosen to have a symmetric distribution.
nodes.statement_short: Under continuity, separation and transversal assumptions, the Lévy measure of a strictly stable element is pi x theta_alpha and its Poisson process is {Gamma_i^{-1/alpha} eps_i}.
nodes.label: thr:levy-k-separating-countable

nodes.name: Integrability condition on $\varepsilon$
nodes.statement: \int_0^\infty \mathbb{E}[1-\mathrm{Re}\,\chi(t\varepsilon)] t^{-(\alpha+1)} \, dt <\infty, \qquad \chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: eq:eps-condition

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.11
nodes.statement:
The measure $
u$ admits the polar decomposition $\pi\otimes	heta_\alpha$ by Theorem~ef{thr:general-polar} applied with $\mathbb{X}:=\mathbb{K}'$, $\mathcal{H} := \{1 - \mathrm{Re}\, \chi: \; \chi \in \hat{\mathbb{K}}\}$, and $
u$ being the L'evy measure of $\xi$. Indeed, \eqref{eq:nu-h-integral} follows from \eqref{eq:lev-mes}, $
u$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous by Lemma~ef{lemma:homogeneous} given that \eqref{Eq:lim-chi-positive} is assumed to hold, and the separating condition imposed on $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ yields \eqref{Eq:nu-support-h}. The Poisson point process with intensity measure $	heta_\alpha$ is obtained as $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}: i\in\mathbb{N}\}$. Thus, the Poisson process on $\mathbb{K}'	imes \mathbb{R}_{++}$ with intensity measure $\pi\otimes	heta_\alpha$ is obtained by marking a Poisson point process $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}: i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ with marks $\{\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ that are i.i.d. copies of a random element $\varepsilon$ in $\mathbb{K}'$ with distribution $\pi$. By \eqref{Eq:levy-condition-pi-general}, the random element $\varepsilon$ satisfies \eqref{eq:eps-condition}. Since $
u$ is the push-forward of $\pi\otimes	heta_\alpha$ under the multiplication map $(x,t)\mapsto tx$, the Poisson process with intensity $
u$ is given by $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i:\; i\in\mathbb{N}\}$. The uniqueness of the L'evy measure yields that $
u$ is symmetric if $\xi$ is symmetric. Then in the proof of Proposition~ef{proposition:renorm} it suffices to replace each set $W_k$ with the union of $W_k$ and its image under the involution to ensure that $\pi$ is a symmetric measure.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 2.15 with H={1-Re chi}, using Lemma 3.10 for homogeneity; mark the Poisson process Gamma_i^{-1/alpha} with i.i.d. marks; symmetrise W_k for the symmetric case.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 2.15
nodes.statement:
The measure $
u$ admits the polar decomposition $\pi\otimes	heta_\alpha$ by Theorem~ef{thr:general-polar} applied with $\mathbb{X}:=\mathbb{K}'$, $\mathcal{H} := \{1 - \mathrm{Re}\, \chi: \; \chi \in \hat{\mathbb{K}}\}$, and $
u$ being the L'evy measure of $\xi$. Indeed, \eqref{eq:nu-h-integral} follows from \eqref{eq:lev-mes}, $
u$ is $\alpha$-homogeneous by Lemma~ef{lemma:homogeneous} given that \eqref{Eq:lim-chi-positive} is assumed to hold, and the separating condition imposed on $\hat{\mathbb{K}}$ yields \eqref{Eq:nu-support-h}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Verify the hypotheses of Theorem 2.15 for H={1-Re chi}.

nodes.name: Marked Poisson construction
nodes.statement: The Poisson point process with intensity measure $\theta_\alpha$ is obtained as $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}: i\in\mathbb{N}\}$. Thus, the Poisson process on $\mathbb{K}'\times \mathbb{R}_{++}$ with intensity measure $\pi\otimes\theta_\alpha$ is obtained by marking a Poisson point process $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}: i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ with marks $\{\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ that are i.i.d. copies of a random element $\varepsilon$ in $\mathbb{K}'$ with distribution $\pi$. By \eqref{Eq:levy-condition-pi-general}, the random element $\varepsilon$ satisfies \eqref{eq:eps-condition}. Since $\nu$ is the push-forward of $\pi\otimes\theta_\alpha$ under the multiplication map $(x,t)\mapsto tx$, the Poisson process with intensity $\nu$ is given by $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i:\; i\in\mathbb{N}\}$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Represent the Poisson process as marked points Gamma_i^{-1/alpha} with marks eps_i.

nodes.name: Symmetric case
nodes.statement: The uniqueness of the L\'evy measure yields that $\nu$ is symmetric if $\xi$ is symmetric. Then in the proof of Proposition~\ref{proposition:renorm} it suffices to replace each set $W_k$ with the union of $W_k$ and its image under the involution to ensure that $\pi$ is a symmetric measure.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrise the sets W_k under the involution to make pi symmetric.

nodes.name: Non-uniqueness of the spectral element
nodes.statement: Note that the random element $\varepsilon$ in Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} is not unique and also is not restricted to belong to the transversal $\mathbb{S}$ from Assumption~\ref{assumption:X}. By rescaling it is always possible to arrange that $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{S}$ a.s., however in this case, the Poisson process with intensity $\nu$ is given by $\{c\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i:\; i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ for a positive scaling constant $c$.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones

nodes.name: Convergence of the LePage series in the symmetric case
nodes.statement: Suppose that the ``L\'evy-Khinchin-It\^o'' decomposition of the strictly $\alpha$-stable random element $\xi$ does not contain any deterministic, Gaussian or idempotent components, so that $\xi$ is the sum of the points in a Poisson process $\{\eta_i : i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, where the sum is appropriately defined by using principal values and compensating terms if necessary, see \cite[Th.~7.2]{dav:mol:zuy08}. Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} establishes that $\{\eta_i : i \in \mathbb{N}\}$ can be constructed as $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i: i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, that is, as randomly scaled i.i.d. copies of a random element $\varepsilon$. Recall that no compensating terms for the sum of the $\eta_i$ are required if $\xi$ is $\alpha$-stable and symmetric. In this case, the Laplace exponent of $\xi$ is given by \begin{displaymath} \varphi(\chi) =\int_{\mathbb{K}'}(1-\chi(x))\,\nu(dx) =\int_{\mathbb{K}'}(1-\mathrm{Re}\,\chi(x))\,\nu(dx)\,, \quad \chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}\,. \end{displaymath} Put \begin{equation} \xi^{(r)} :=\sum_{\Gamma_i\leq r} \Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i\,,\qquad r>0. \end{equation} The probability generating functional formula for a Poisson point process yields that, for all $\chi\in\hat{\mathbb{K}}$, \begin{align*} \mathbb{E} \chi(\xi^{(r)}) & =\exp\left\{-\int_{r^{-\alpha}}^\infty \int_{\mathbb{K}'} (1-\chi(tx))\alpha t^{-(\alpha+1)} \, \pi(dx) \, dt\right\}\\ & \to \mathbb{E} \chi(\xi)\qquad \text{as } r\uparrow\infty, \end{align*} since $\mathbb{E}\chi(t\varepsilon)$ is real-valued by the symmetry of $\varepsilon$ and the integral under the exponential converges by \eqref{eq:eps-condition}.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.statement_short: For symmetric xi, the truncated LePage sums xi^(r) have Laplace transforms converging to that of xi.

nodes.name: Truncated LePage sum
nodes.statement: \xi^{(r)} :=\sum_{\Gamma_i\leq r} \Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i\,,\qquad r>0.
nodes.section: 3 Strictly stable random elements on convex cones
nodes.label: eq:xi-r

nodes.name: Euclidean space R^d
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}^d$ with the usual arithmetic addition, the involution given by the negation, the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and conventional scaling by positive scalars, then Assumption~\ref{assumption:X} holds with $\mathbb{S}$ being the sphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to any norm. A countable separating family of continuous characters is given by $\chi(x)=\exp\{\imath \langle u,x\rangle\}$, where $\langle u,x\rangle$ is the scalar product of $u\in\mathbb{Q}^d$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} yields the polar representation of L\'evy measures for strictly stable random vectors. In particular, each strictly stable random vector $\xi$ corresponds to the Poisson process $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i:i\in\mathbb{N}\}$. If $\alpha\in(0,1)$ or if $\xi$ is symmetric, then the sum of these points converges almost surely and yields the LePage series decomposition of $\xi$, see \cite{lep:wood:zin81}.
nodes.label: example:Rd

nodes.name: Operator stable random vectors
nodes.statement: In the setting of Example~\ref{example:Rd}, define the scaling by letting $tx:=\exp\{(\log t)\mathbf{A}\}x$, $t>0$, for a non-degenerate matrix $\mathbf{A}$. The corresponding stable elements are usually called \emph{operator stable}, see \cite{hud:mas81,shar69}. An operator stable random element is infinitely divisible and so admits a series representation and a L\'evy measure. By Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable}, an operator stable random element $\xi$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits the LePage series representation \begin{displaymath} \xi\overset{d}{\sim} \sum_{i\in\mathbb{N}} \exp\{-\alpha^{-1}(\log\Gamma_i)\mathbf{A}\} \varepsilon_i. \end{displaymath} Note that the polar decomposition of the L\'evy measure appears in \cite[Eq.~(2)]{hud:jur:veeh86} and \cite{hud:mas81}.
nodes.label: ex:operator

nodes.name: Real-valued stochastic processes
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family $\mathbb{R}^{[0,\infty)}$ of real valued-functions on $\mathbb{R}_+$ with the cylindrical $\sigma$-algebra, the pointwise arithmetic addition of functions as the semigroup operation, involution being the negation, and the scaling operation applied pointwise. It is known \cite{kab:stoev12,mar70} that an infinitely divisible separable in probability stochastic process $\xi(s)$, $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$, can be associated with the Poisson process $\{\eta_i,i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ on $\mathbb{R}^{[0,\infty)}$ with a $\sigma$-finite intensity measure $
u$, so that $\xi$ admits a L'evy measure $
u$. If $\xi$ is symmetric, then, for each $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$,  egin{equation} \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \lim_{r\downarrow 0}\sum_{|\eta_i(t)|\geq r} \eta_i(s),\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+, \end{equation} where $\overset{d}{\sim}$ in this setting denotes the equality of all finite-dimensional distributions. It should be noted that the order of summands in \eqref{eq:id-processes} may change with $t$, and there might be no order of the summands that guarantees the convergence for all rational $s$, not to say for all $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$. Such a common order exists for random functions with non-negative values (in which case $\mathbb{K}$ is endowed with the identical involution). This cone does not admit a countable separating family of characters. Let $	ilde{\mathbb{K}}$ be the countable family of characters defined by  egin{equation} \chi(x)=e^{\imath x(s) u},\qquad s\in\mathbb{Q}_+, \end{equation} where $x=(x(s))_{s\geq 0}$ is an element of $\mathbb{R}^{[0,\infty)}$ and $u$ belongs to the set $\mathbb{Q}$ of rational numbers. Theorem~ef{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} applies to the process $\xi$ restricted onto the set $\mathbb{Q}_+$ of non-negative rationals, so that the image $	ilde{
u}$ of the L'evy measure $
u$ under the map that restricts a function to $\mathbb{Q}_+$ has polar decomposition as $\pi\otimes	heta_\alpha$ and the Poisson process with intensity $	ilde{
u}$ is given by $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}	ilde{\varepsilon}_i,i\geq1\}$. By \cite[Prop.~2.19]{kab:stoev12}, for each $t\in\mathbb{R}_+\setminus\mathbb{Q}_+$, the separability property of $\xi$ yields that $\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}	ilde{\varepsilon}_i(t_n)$ converges in probability to $\eta_i(t)$, whence $	ilde{\varepsilon}_i(t_n)$ converges in probability to $\varepsilon_i(t):=\Gamma_i^{1/\alpha}\eta_i(t)$. Thus, the L'evy measure $
u$ corresponds to the Poisson process $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i,i\geq1\}$, where $\{\varepsilon_i,i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. separable processes distributed as $\varepsilon(s)$, $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$. Condition \eqref{eq:eps-condition} in this setting is equivalent to $\mathbb{E}|\varepsilon(s)|^\alpha<\infty$ for all $s$. In the symmetric case, following \eqref{eq:xi-r}, the convergence in \eqref{eq:id-processes} can be rephrased as  egin{displaymath} \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \lim_{r\uparrow\infty} \sum_{\Gamma_i\leq r} \Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i(s),\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+. \end{displaymath} Therefore, in case of symmetric $\alpha$-stable processes the order of summands in \eqref{eq:id-processes} can be made the same for all time points. This makes it possible to appeal to path regularity results for stochastic integrals from \cite[Th.~4]{ros89p} in order to confirm that $\varepsilon$ shares path regularity properties with $\xi$, for instance, $\varepsilon$ is almost surely right-continuous with left limits (c\`adl\`ag) if $\xi$ is c\`adl\`ag. The same holds for stochastic processes with almost surely non-negative values, since then the involution is the identity. The pointwise convergence of the LePage series yields the uniform convergence, see \cite{bas:ros13}. Note that a result concerning the existence of the series representation of a general (not necessarily symmetric stable) infinitely divisible c\`adl\`ag function using c\`adl\`ag summands is not available.
nodes.statement_short: For separable processes on R_+, restrict to rationals, apply Theorem 3.11, and extend; in the symmetric case the LePage series converges with a common order.
nodes.label: ex:processes-values

nodes.name: Max-stable processes
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family of non-negative functions $x(s)$, $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$, with the cylindrical $\sigma$-algebra, the semigroup operation being pointwise maximum, identical involution, and the scaling applied poinwisely to the values of the function. It is shown in \cite{kab:stoev12} that each separable max-infinitely divisible stochastic process admits a L\'evy measure. A separating family of characters is given by those of the form $x \mapsto \chi(x) = \mathbf{1}_{x(s)< a}$ for $s,a\in\mathbb{R}_+$. While these characters are not continuous, the function $t\mapsto \chi(tx)$ is right-continuous. Restricting the functions to non-negative rationals as in Example~\ref{ex:processes-values} and using the results from \cite{kab:stoev12} concerning the max-infinitely divisible setting, we obtain that the L\'evy measure of each max-stable separable in probability stochastic process $\xi$ admits a polar representation and the process itself admits the series representation \begin{displaymath} \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \bigvee_{i\in\mathbb{N}}\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i(s), \end{displaymath} which first appeared in \cite{haan84}.

nodes.name: Time-stable processes
nodes.statement: Equip the family $\mathbb{K}$ of real-valued c\`adl\`ag functions on $\mathbb{R}_+$ that vanish at the origin with pointwise arithmetic addition, involution being the negation, and the scaling defined by $(tx)(s):=x(ts)$, $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$, for $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$. Stable elements in this cone with $\alpha=1$ are called \emph{time-stable} processes in \cite{kop:mol15} and {\em processes infinitely divisible with respect to time} in \cite{man05}. The characters are given by \eqref{Eq:chi-line} and, in view of the c\`adl\`ag assumption, they constitute a countable separating family and are right-continuous as required in Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable}. Furthermore, $\chi(tx)=\exp\{\imath x(ts)u\}\to 1$ as $t\downarrow0$, so that a transversal in $\mathbb{K}$ can be constructed as in Remark~\ref{rem:sphere-from-h}, see also \cite{kop:mol15}. Thus, if a time-stable process with symmetric distribution admits a series representation with c\`adl\`ag functions, it also admits the LePage representation \begin{displaymath} \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \sum_{i\in\mathbb{N}} \varepsilon_i(\Gamma_i^{-1}s),\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+, \end{displaymath} where $\{\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ are i.i.d. copies of $\varepsilon(s)$, $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$, such that \begin{displaymath} \mathbb{E} \int_0^\infty \min(1,\varepsilon(s)^2)s^{-2}ds<\infty \end{displaymath} because of \eqref{eq:eps-condition}. The setting can be altered by considering the family of non-negative c\`adl\`ag functions with the identical involution. In particular, each seperable in probability c\`adl\`ag time-stable process with non-negative values admits a LePage series representation.
nodes.label: ex:time-stable

nodes.name: Locally finite random measures
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family of locally finite measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the arithmetic addition, identical involution, and the Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by the vague topology \cite[Sec.~9.1]{MR2371524}. An infinitely divisible locally finite random measure admits a L\'evy measure, see \cite{MR2371524}. A countable separating family of continuous characters consists of \begin{displaymath} \chi(\mu)=\exp\left\{-\int ud\mu\right\}, \end{displaymath} where $u$ belongs to an appropriately chosen countable family of continuous functions with compact support. If the scaling operation is applied to the values of measures, then $\chi(tx)\to1$ as $t\downarrow0$ for all $x$, so that a transversal can be constructed as in Remark~\ref{rem:sphere-from-h}. An alternative way of constructing a measurable trasversal $\mathbb{S}$ is to take a sequence $\{B_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ of bounded sets that form a base of the topology and let $\mu\in\mathbb{S}$ if $\mu(B_0)=\cdots=\mu(B_{n-1})=0$ and $\mu(B_n)=1$ for some $n$. By Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable}, each stable locally finite random measure admits the LePage representation \begin{displaymath} \mu\overset{d}{\sim} \sum_{i\in\mathbb{N}} \Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i \end{displaymath} for a sequence $\{\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ of i.i.d. locally finite measures with $\alpha$-integrable values.

nodes.name: Union-stable random closed sets
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family of closed sets $F$ in $\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}$ with the union as the semigroup operation, identical involution, the conventional scaling, and the $\sigma$-algebra generated by families $\{F:F\cap K\neq\emptyset\}$ for all compact sets $K$. The countable separating family of continuous characters is given by $\chi(F):=\mathbf{1}_{F\cap G=\emptyset}$ for open sets $G$ from the base of topology on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Note that deterministic closed sets have idempotent distributions in this cone. It is known that each union infinitely divisible random closed set admits a L\'evy measure, see \cite{MR2132405}. Thus, each strictly $\alpha$-stable random closed set $\xi$ without idempotent factors (so that $\mathbb{P}\{x\in \xi\}<1$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$) admits the series representation as the union of $\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i$, $i\in\mathbb{N}$, for a sequence $\{\varepsilon_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ of i.i.d. random closed sets.

nodes.name: Random capacities
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family of all non-decreasing functions $\Phi:\mathcal{K}\mapsto\mathbb{R}_+$ defined on the family $\mathcal{K}$ of compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that vanish at the empty set and are upper semicontinuous, that is $\Phi(K_n)\downarrow\Phi(K)$ as $K_n\downarrow K$. Such functions are known as capacities (and sometimes are called topological pre-capacities, see \cite{MR1814344}). Equip $\mathbb{K}$ with the semigroup operation by taking pointwise maximum of two capacities and the scaling of their values. It is shown in \cite{nor86} that an infinitely divisible capacity $\xi$ admits a L\'evy measure. It does not have idempotent factors if the essential infimum of $\xi(K)$ vanishes for all $K\in\mathcal{K}$. By Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable}, each strictly $\alpha$-stable capacity admits the series representation $\sum_{i \in \mathbb{N}} \Gamma^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i$, see also \cite[Th.~4.1]{mol:strok15}.

nodes.name: Metric measure spaces
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family of metric measure spaces with the Cartesian product as the semigroup operation and the scaling applied to the metric, see \cite{evan:mol15} for details. This semigroup admits a countable separating family of characters and a measurable transversal. Furthermore, each infinitely divisible random element in $\mathbb{K}$ admits a L\'evy measure and so Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} applies and yields the LePage series representation of stable metric measure spaces obtained in \cite[Th.~10.3]{evan:mol15}.

nodes.name: Series representation of infinitely divisible processes
nodes.statement: \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \lim_{r\downarrow 0}\sum_{|\eta_i(t)|\geq r} \eta_i(s),\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+,
nodes.label: eq:id-processes

nodes.name: Characters for function spaces
nodes.statement: \chi(x)=e^{\imath x(s) u},\qquad s\in\mathbb{Q}_+,
nodes.label: Eq:chi-line
